title: heterogeneous-quantization-compatibility-bench-and-gate-2026
author: Aisha Patel
body:
Summary:
This playbook documents the benchmarking harness, pass/fail gating criteria, and rollout procedures for deploying heterogeneous quantized model variants across the Redwood serving runtime. It covers functional compatibility checks, latency/throughput regressions, scheduler interactions, and trace/telemetry expectations when enabling INT8/INT4/mixed quantized kernels across different accelerator families.

Context and motivation:
- Quantization reduces per-token cost but interacts with kernel selection, KV cache semantics, and scheduler admission.
- Different hardware (A100, H100, A10G, RTX series) and driver/toolkit combinations expose subtle numerical and perf differences.
- We need an automated, reproducible bench and gate so that quantized rollouts do not cause silent quality regressions or operational instability.

Scope:
- Model families: decoder-only LLMs currently in serving fleet (7B–70B variants).
- Quant schemes: symmetric asymmetric INT8, dynamic/quant-aware INT4, group-wise per-channel scales, and mixed fp16/INT8 kernels.
- Hardware: NVIDIA A100 (40/80GB), H100 (80GB), A10G, and representative on-prem RTX6000-class nodes.
- Runtime surfaces: kernel selection path, KV cache behavior, session warmstart, scheduler handoff.

Bench objectives and primary metrics:
- Correctness: token-level output equivalence check (soft) against fp16 baseline using perplexity and distributional drift metrics. Gate: top-1 token divergence <= 0.8% and log-prob drift RMS <= 0.12.
- Latency: p50/p95/p99 for generation with 32-token completions. Gate: p95 <= baseline_p95 + 12ms on same hardware class.
- Throughput: tokens/sec under continuous steady-state. Gate: throughput drop <= 15% vs baseline for same sequence-length distribution.
- Resource safety: GPU memory delta, peak SM utilization, and thermal/power events. Gate: memory overhead <= +2GB for same shard placement; no thermal throttling during 1h soak.
- Scheduler impact: admission/queue time distribution and preemption events. Gate: queue-time p95 regression <= 10ms and preempt rate increase <= 0.5 percentage points.

Test harness and reproducibility:
- All bench runs are executed through the bench-orchestrator container with version-tagged artifacts. Typical CLI:
  ./bench-orchestrator run --suite quant-compat --model gpt-redwood-13b --variant int8-symmetric --hw a100-80 --seed 42 --duration 3600 --trace true

- Example orchestration config (YAML) used for reproducible runs (presented as plain text):
  ---
  suite: quant-compat
  model: gpt-redwood-13b
  variants: [fp16, int8-symmetric, int4-mixed]
  hardware: [a100-80, a10g, h100-80]
  sequence_profile: "web-chat-32-32"
  duration_seconds: 3600
  traffic_shape: "steady"
  trace_level: "full"
  metrics_to_collect: [latency, throughput, logprobs, kernel_signals, scheduler_telemetry]
  ---

Workload definitions (catalog):
- web-chat-32-32: prompt len=32, gen len=32, 1 request per second per client, 200 clients.
- long-infer-128: prompt len=128, gen len=128, low concurrency (20 clients), used to stress KV cache.
- bursty-batch: synthetic burst bursts to validate admission controller and kernel preemption.

Hardware matrix (table):
| hardware | driver | cuda | cudnn | notes |
| A100-80 | 525.60 | 11.8 | 8.4 | baseline fleet node |
| H100-80 | 535.54 | 12.1 | 8.5 | large-model heavy kernel variants |
| A10G | 520.56 | 11.7 | 8.3 | cost-optimized host |
| RTX6000 | 515.43 | 11.6 | 8.2 | on-prem reference |

Quantization profiles exercised (examples):
- int8-symmetric: per-tensor symmetric scales, fused matmul-kernel path.
- int8-perchannel: per-output channel scales, preferred for grouped conv-like operations in some kernels.
- int4-mixed: kv cache keys stored in INT8, weights int4 with fp16 accumulation for matmuls.
- dynamic-qat: quantization-aware fine-tuning enabled with 128-step calibration.

Quality and numerical checks (procedure):
1. Run correctness harness on a 2k-sample reference corpus (reserved eval set). Collect logits, prefix logprobs, and argmax tokens.
2. Compute metrics: token divergence (fraction of tokens where argmax changes), KL divergence of softmax distributions, and RMS log-prob drift.
3. If token divergence > 0.8% OR KL > 0.05 OR RMS drift > 0.12, mark the variant FAILED and abort rollout.

Performance and operational checks (procedure):
1. Warmup: run 15-minute warmup under workload profile. Verify KV cache warm-up completion and shader JIT stabilization.
2. Soak: 1-hour steady-state run. Capture p50/p95/p99 latency, tokens/sec, GPU memory, and scheduler traces.
3. Failure modes monitored: out-of-memory, kernel launch timeouts, driver resets, and excessive preempt/backpressure events.
4. If any hard failure occurs (OOM, driver reset), variant is FAILED automatically.

Scheduler interaction tests (special):
- Run mixed cohort where 20% of requests use quantized variant and 80% use fp16 to validate admission controller smoothing. Observe admission tokens/sec variance and kernel handoff latency.
- Inject synthetic priority inversion by marking high-priority low-latency requests during burst windows; measure end-to-end impact.

Acceptance gates and rollout matrix:
- Canary (10% traffic, single region): pass all correctness checks, p95 <= baseline_p95+12ms, thermal/power stable.
- Regional wave (50% traffic across 2 AZs): no more than 0.5% customer-visible error increase during 24h, scheduler preempt increase <= 0.5pp.
- Fleet roll (100%): no regressions observed in 72h aggregated metrics; manual sign-off by runtime and SRE owners.

Rollout checklist (numbered steps):
1. Validate bench artifacts and record full trace URLs in the release ticket.
2. Run local preflight on representative dev nodes (10 minutes).
3. Submit canary binary and kernel hints to canary pool.
4. Monitor canary with enhanced telemetry (kernel-level traces, perf counters, trace-sampling=10%).
5. If canary passes 12h check, advance to regional wave, else rollback immediately using kernel rollback playbook.
6. Post regional wave soak, check quality regressions with reference eval set.
7. Fleet roll and final sign-off.

Observability and traces to collect (minimum):
- kernel_id, kernel_variant, kernel_duration_ms, kernel_queue_time_ms
- kvcache_warmup_percent, kvcache_miss_rate, kvcache_eviction_count
- preempt_event_count, admission_queue_time_ms, scheduling_slot_id
- per-token logprob delta (sampled 0.5% of requests)

Automated alarms (suggested):
- token_divergence_rate > 0.8% over a 30-minute window -> Pager -> owners: runtime-team@s.redwood.ai
- p95 latency regression > 12ms for 10-minute window -> Pager -> owners: sre-oncall@s.redwood.ai
- OOM or driver-reset event count > 1 in 1 hour -> Immediate rollback and incident creation.

Ownership and escalation:
- Bench harness owner: Performance Engineering (Primary: Marco Nguyen).
- Rollout owner: Runtime Releases (Primary: Elena Karpova).
- Oncall escalation: Eng-SRE -> Runtime leads -> Applied ML if model quality suspicion.

Appendix A: Example analysis commands
- Extract top divergent prompts:
  python scripts/analysis/top_divergent_prompts.py --baseline traces/fp16-run.json --variant traces/int8-run.json --out reports/divergent.csv
- Kernel-level flamegraph generation:
  perf-kernel-collector --input traces/kernel-events.ndjson --output flame.svg --group-by kernel_variant

Appendix B: Known caveats and mitigation notes
- Some older driver stacks return non-deterministic host-side rounding for INT4 accumulators; avoid enabling int4-mixed on nodes with driver < 520.70.
- KV cache pointer packing in int4 modes increases reconstruction cost during warmstart; add an extra warmup pass for long-infer workloads.
- Scheduler fairness heuristics may favor fp16 kernels due to lower variance; ensure admission controller accounts for measured variance in tokens/sec estimates.
